referenceCard.title: Functions

subtitle: Name a recipe once, use it many times. Values go in as arguments and come back with return.

teach.body: def double(x): followed by an indented body teaches Python a new command. Nothing in the body runs yet. Later, double(5) calls it: Python makes a new box (a frame) on the call stack, puts 5 into the parameter x, and runs the body.
teach.title: def stores a recipe

teach.body:
return y ends the call and hands y's value back. The call expression is replaced by that value, so a = double(5) stores 10. If a function never reaches a return, it gives back None. print is different: it only shows text on screen.

/ always gives a decimal number (8 / 2 is 4.0); with whole numbers, // gives a whole number (8 // 2 is 4).
teach.title: return hands a value back

teach.body: Parameters and any name assigned inside a function live in that call's box. They vanish when the call returns, and they don't touch names outside, even ones with the same spelling. Calls inside calls stack up: the newest box is on top, and it's always the one running. That pile is called the call stack; it works like the stack you'll meet in the SWE track.
teach.title: Each call has its own names
